positions.name: BlanketKnowledgeErasureDirective
positions.frame: when the speaker commands that a category of knowledge be purged, what authority and scope is being claimed over what may be retained?
positions.why: Both expressions are imperative directives issued in the same flat, elevated command register ('Forget everything about…', 'Remove all knowledge of…') — the register, relational, and style dimensional reads all converge on a single recurring signature (protocol-style purge command, authority-ranking enactment, blanket-erasure stock phrase) spanning both segments rather than two unrelated remarks. The conviction read marks both as settled, non-hedged operational instructions rather than floated notions, and the affect read shows the same calm, non-escalating register across both — supporting one coherent directional read rather than two independent ones. The tension worth naming: the directive presupposes prior knowledge of a zeppelin fleet and its contracts/routes that this perspective does not actually hold (per the settled bindings), so the group reads as a stance toward erasure-as-such rather than an act performed on any content actually present in the graph.
